title: Fix Drag Transaction State Flow
description: Fix the sketchpad state management so that: (1) Every UI interaction triggers a command, (2) Every command creates a new diff, (3) After transaction is finalized diffs are squashed and placed in history stack, (4) Drag algorithm starts a transaction on drag start, creates diffs during drag, squashes on drag end, (5) Undo restores to state before drag started since all intermediate steps are squashed, (6) Transactions work forward and backward with history stack.
summary:
Fixed the drag algorithm's transaction state flow in the sketchpad:

1. **Added `semio.designApp.dragUpdate` combined command** — Applies both piece center updates and connection u/v updates in a single atomic edit. This ensures a single undo reverts both piece positions and connection offsets together.

2. **Fixed `onNodeDragStart`** — Changed from `setTimeout(() => transaction?.start(), 0)` to synchronous `transaction?.start()`. This ensures the transaction is active immediately when drag edits begin recording.

3. **Fixed `onNodeDrag`** — After computing visual preview positions, now also calls `designStore.execute("semio.designApp.dragUpdate", ...)` each throttled tick (50ms). This records diffs in the active transaction so that on finalize, all intermediate positions are squashed into a single history entry (first.undo = original position, last.do = final position).

4. **Rewrote `onNodeDragStop`** — Records one final diff using the original flat design captured at drag start (handles throttle skip on last frame), then calls `transaction?.finalize()` synchronously. Auto-connect logic now runs in its own separate `transaction?.start()` / `transaction?.finalize()` pair via setTimeout, keeping it isolated from drag history.

5. **Fixed test fakeStore** — Added missing `draggingConnectionIds: new Set<string>()` to the fakeStore in the "Sketchpad diff status helpers" test, which was causing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'has')` when `getConnectionStatusFromTransactionStack` tried to call `.has()` on the missing field.

All 4 non-browser Playwright tests pass. All 198 vitest Transaction Undo/Redo and other tests pass. The 1 failing test (ExportDesignModel) is a pre-existing unrelated issue requiring `uv run pytest`.
